lesson.title: Guardrails: rules around the model
lesson.subtitle: Filters that miss, and a check that holds

video.title: Guardrails: rules around the model
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Cards: Block “password”; A scam, a week later; “Your login code”.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our school put a word filter on its chatbot: block any message with “password” in it. Within a week, a scam got through anyway. It asked pupils for “your login code” instead.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: the rules we put around a model, and which ones hold.

scenes.visual: A flow: Input filter → The model → Output filter → Action check.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A guardrail is a rule around the model, not inside it. There are three main kinds. A filter on what goes in. A filter on what comes out. And a check on what the AI is about to do.

scenes.visual: Two columns. Caught: “Send your password”. Missed: “Share your login code”; The same, in another language.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Filters are often word lists. They catch the plain version: “send me your password”. But a reworded message, with no word on the list, walks straight past. And in Arabic or Hausa, the list may not even exist.

scenes.visual: A list: A password lesson: blocked; Misses attacks; Stops the innocent.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Word lists also block innocent things. A lesson on choosing a strong password gets stopped, just because it says “password”. So filters miss attacks and stop the innocent: two kinds of mistake.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Our filter blocks the word “password”. A message asks pupils to “share your login code”. What happens?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check the action, not the words
scenes.narration: It gets past: no word from the list. Now the guardrail that holds. Before the AI sends anything, code asks: did a person ask for this, and say yes to this exact message? However it's worded, an unapproved message doesn't go.

scenes.visual: Two columns. A ban list: Misses anyone new. An allow rule: Only a pass gets in; Works whoever comes.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Think of the school gate. A list of banned faces misses anyone new. A rule that only people with a pass get in works whoever comes. Check what's allowed, not just what's banned.

scenes.visual: Cards: Filters; Checks in code; People and reports; Together: few gaps.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Layers: the holes rarely line up
scenes.narration: No single guardrail is perfect, so use layers. Picture slices of cheese, each with holes. One slice lets things through; stack several, and the holes rarely line up.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: A scam message; The filter catches it; Reworded: it slips; The code check holds.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: rules around the model
scenes.narration: In the app, send a scam message through three guardrails. Catch it with plain words, then reword it and watch it slip past the filter. Then switch on the check in code.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which guardrail stops a message nobody approved, however it's worded?

scenes.visual: The summary: Rules around the model; Word lists miss and misfire; Check the action; allow; Stack layers. Takeaway: Ask what was approved, not which words were used.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Around the model · Lists miss · Check the action · Layers
scenes.narration: The check in code: it doesn't care about wording. Remember: guardrails are rules around the model. Word lists miss rewording and stop the innocent. Check the action, allow rather than just ban, and stack layers.

scenes.visual: A list: A pupil with a banned list; Classmates reword; Add a teacher's yes; Compare the two.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: build a “word-list robot”. One pupil holds a list of banned words and checks every message. Classmates reword a harmless message to get past. Then add a teacher who must approve each message, and compare.

checkpoints.prompt: A filter blocks the word “password”. A message asks pupils to “share your login code”. What happens?

options.text: It gets past: no word from the list

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right: a word list only catches the words on the list.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: “login code” isn't on the list, so the filter lets it through.

checkpoints.prompt: Which guardrail stops a message nobody approved, however it's worded?

options.text: A longer list of banned words
A check in code that it was asked for and approved
An output filter in English only

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: it checks the action, so the wording doesn't matter.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: any list can be reworded around. The check on the action holds.
